articles.title: Magic Tree House author Mary Pope Osborne has donated more than 1.2 million books to children in underserved US schools through her Gift of Books programme
articles.summary: For many children, a book can be their first opportunity to explore places, people and experiences beyond their immediate surroundings.
articles.body: For many children, a book can be their first opportunity to explore places, people and experiences beyond their immediate surroundings. But access to reading material is not the same for every family, and schools serving low-income communities often have to work with limited resources. Mary Pope Osborne, the author behind the popular Magic Tree House series, has spent years addressing that gap. Alongside a writing career spanning more than three decades, she has supported children's literacy through a personal book-giving initiative. Her Gift of Books programme has now helped place more than 1.2 million books with children attending underserved Title I schools across the United States, as per Mary Pope Osborne Classroom Adventures Program.Mary Pope Osborne's writing career began with a childhood interest in make-believeOsborne's connection with storytelling goes back well before the publication of her first children's books. Growing up in a military family meant moving frequently. By the time she was 15, she had lived in several parts of the United States, as well as Austria. Her family eventually settled in North Carolina after her father retired, but the young Osborne still missed the changing surroundings that had shaped much of her early life.She found a different kind of escape at a local community theatre. After discovering the venue, she began spending much of her free time acting and helping backstage. It was there that she became interested in the possibilities of performance and storytelling, although her academic interests later took her in another direction.At the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Osborne initially studied drama before switching to religion. Her interest in mythology and comparative religion introduced her to stories and traditions from different cultures.How travelling through Asia shaped Mary Pope Osborne's early lifeAfter graduating in the early 1970s, Osborne spent several years travelling and working in different places. As reported, she travelled through 16 Asian countries, including India, Nepal, Afghanistan, Iran and Pakistan, as part of an overland journey with a group of young Europeans. The experience was not without difficulties. An earthquake in northern Afghanistan and a riot in Kabul placed the group in danger, while a serious infection eventually brought her travels to an end in Kathmandu.During her hospital stay in Nepal, she read Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings trilogy. The experience of reading about an imaginary world while looking out towards the Himalayas remained connected in her memory with that period of travel.When she returned to the United States, Osborne took on several jobs, including working as a window dresser, medical assistant and Russian travel consultant. She later moved into New York City's theatre and publishing circles, taking work as a waitress, bartender, acting teacher and assistant editor for a children's magazine.Her personal life also took an important turn during this period. She met actor and musician Will Osborne at a musical about Jesse James in Washington, DC. The couple married a year later in New York City.The Magic Tree House series became her best-known workOsborne's writing career began with a story drawn partly from her own childhood. She wrote about an 11-year-old girl growing up in the American South, using experiences that reflected aspects of her early life. The manuscript eventually became her first young adult novel, Run, Run as Fast as You Can.From there, she developed a varied body of work covering children's fiction, biographies, picture books, mysteries, mythology and folklore. Her writing has also explored subjects such as world religions and stories inspired by Homer's Odyssey.The project that brought her the widest readership, however, was Magic Tree House. The series follows Jack and Annie, two children who travel through different historical periods and places using a mysterious tree house. Their adventures introduce young readers to historical figures, cultures and events through accessible fiction.Osborne has written 64 fiction titles in the series, including the Merlin Missions, along with a Super Edition. The books have taken the two central characters to encounters with figures such as Mozart and Louis Armstrong, as well as journeys through different periods of history.Her husband, Will, and her sister, Natalie Pope Boyce, have also worked on the franchise. Together, they have developed the accompanying Magic Tree House Fact Trackers, a nonfiction collection that provides additional information related to the subjects explored in the stories. The companion series has grown to 36 books.A personal book programme has reached children in underserved schoolsAway from the fictional journeys of Jack and Annie, Osborne has devoted considerable attention to a more immediate issue: whether children have access to books in their classrooms. Her Gift of Books programme has distributed more than 1.2 million books to children in underserved Title I schools across the United States. Title I is a federal education programme that provides financial assistance to schools serving communities with high numbers of children from low-income families.The initiative reflects Osborne's involvement in literacy beyond her work as an author. Rather than limiting her contribution to writing stories for young readers, she has used her own resources to help get books directly into the hands of children who might otherwise have fewer opportunities to build personal reading collections.The scale of the programme also places it among the longer-running parts of her public work. Osborne has continued to support school visits and literacy discussions, drawing on her experience as a writer to engage with pupils, teachers and parents.Her literacy advocacy has extended beyond the United StatesOsborne's work on children's reading has also taken her to international platforms. She has spoken at the United Nations about the importance of literacy around the world and has visited schools in the United States and other countries to discuss reading and education.Her efforts received wider television attention when she was profiled on NBC's Rock Center with Brian Williams. The programme highlighted her continuing involvement in children's literacy and the work she had undertaken alongside her publishing career.Between 1993 and 1997, Osborne also served as president of the Authors Guild, one of the leading professional organisations representing published authors in the United States. The position added an industry dimension to her work, placing her among those involved in representing writers and their interests. She has received recognition for her writing, with more than 100 books published across different genres for children and young adults. Yet her public work has not been confined to literary achievements or professional roles.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Dana, please take the job!’: Trump offers UFC chief White House press secy post
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has offered Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White the position of White House press secretary, weeks
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has offered Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White the position of White House press secretary, weeks after Katie Zacharia exited the post following a turbulent five-day tenure. Urging White to accept the role, Trump also asked him to bring several prominent mixed martial arts fighters along as his assistants.In a post on his social media platform Truth Social on Saturday, Trump described White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior” and said he wanted him to take charge of the White House press operation.“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote.The president also named six fighters he wanted White to bring with him, including Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harris.“I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris,” Trump said.Concluding his announcement, Trump expressed confidence that White would bring a different approach to the administration's communication strategy.“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!” he wrote, signing off as “President DONALD J. TRUMP”.White, who has led the UFC for more than two decades, has maintained a close relationship with Trump, regularly appearing alongside the president at major events. Their association reached a new milestone in June when the UFC staged UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of American independence.The development comes amid a wider reshuffle of Trump's inner circle following significant Republican losses in the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats make gains in Congress and challenge the administration's political position.Trump recently announced that Stephen Miller, the administration's hardline immigration architect, would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff from Monday, November 9.The proposed appointment comes amid a series of changes in the White House press office. Karoline Leavitt stepped down as press secretary in August, saying she wanted to focus on raising her two young children. Her departure came shortly before the crucial midterm elections.Trump subsequently appointed Katie Zacharia to the position. Katie's tenure lasted just five days before she was removed on October 16 after a widely criticised first briefing. Her debut press conference lasted less than 15 minutes and featured only three questions from reporters.The president subsequently indicated that he had advised her to reconsider the appointment. “I said, 'Is this for you, Katie? Because honestly, you don't need this',” he told reporters, adding, “You don't have to be treated this badly.”Zacharia later praised Trump on X, describing him as “kind, wonderful, gracious, thoughtful, enthusiastic, and the most hardworking man”.White's response to Trump's offer remains awaited.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iran says forces 'stronger' than at beginning of war
articles.summary: Iran said on Saturday its military had grown stronger since the outset of the war with the United States, as mediators including Qatar worked to prevent any...
articles.body:
Iran said on Saturday its military had grown stronger since the outset of the war with the United States, as mediators including Qatar worked to prevent any return to fighting after months of deadlock in the conflict.

Washington also offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran's nuclear programme.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Instagram on Saturday that over the past 48 hours he held phone calls with ministers from 12 countries.

US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on Friday to discuss efforts to end the war.

Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani applauded colleagues in the US administration for "genuine intentions to find a way to contain the situation and to de-escalate it".

"Thanks also to some wise voices in Tehran, we have prevented that from getting out of control," he said in Oxford on Friday.

Trump said Iran -- which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war -- is eager to end the conflict.

"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.

The US leader previously talked up the possibility of resuming heavy strikes on Iran but has since walked back from the idea.

Nevertheless, the US military has conducted occasional limited strikes.

Late on Saturday, the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions on the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz, hours after two earlier explosions were reported and the military said it had shot down a drone over the island.

Washington last attacked Qeshm on Tuesday.

The Middle East conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.

Tehran has since sought to limit traffic through Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said the strategic waterway would remain closed until Tehran's demands were met by Washington.

He also said Iran's forces "are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war".

"They now possess greater motivation, commitment and self-confidence," he added, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.

"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective and without geographical limitations."

Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi told Fars news agency on Saturday that "the increase in the range of Iran's missiles continues steadily".

He spoke days after Trump's Republican Party suffered heavy losses in midterm elections widely viewed as a referendum on the US leader's turbulent second term.

Ali Vaez, of the International Crisis Group, told AFP that "having suffered electoral defeat and failed to secure military victory, Trump is unlikely to tolerate the trifecta of diplomatic humiliation".

"The midterms have raised the political cost of war, but a lame duck Trump could become a flame duck if Iran denies him a face-saving exit," he added.

"Both sides may be mistaking the other's weakness for a reason to hold out rather than compromise."

Qatar's prime minister said "we cannot... just wait for this moment of a perfect deal" as there would never be one.

He added that priority should be given to addressing the nuclear issue and ensuring freedom of navigation and the security of the Gulf.

Iran's military said in a statement carried by state TV on Saturday that a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz "caught fire and came to a halt after striking a naval mine".

The US had recently said all mines had been cleared from the waterway.

On Friday, the US military said it was offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

Rewards for Justice, a State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including "facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," US Central Command said on X.

Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran's nuclear programme.

"If we didn't hit Iran, you wouldn't have Israel today," he said on Friday.

"If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East."

articles.title: Fine Gael: Irish unity forum proposed in party conference
articles.summary: The plans come as part of Fine Gael's "blueprint" on Irish unity, which was published at their ard fheis.
articles.body:
Fine Gael has proposed appointing a junior minister in the Irish government for "north south relations" as well as establishing a forum on Irish unity.

The plans come as part of the party's long awaited "blueprint" on Irish unity, which was published at Fine Gael's ard fheis (party conference) in Cork on Saturday.

It comes just days after Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheal Martin, the leader of Fianna Fáil, put forward his own proposals on Irish unity to his parliamentary party.

He proposed setting up a new "initiative" on the constitutional future of the island of Ireland.

The two parties are both in a coalition government together, supported by a number of Independent TDs (members of the Irish parliament) in Dublin.

Fine Gael party leader and Tánaiste (deputy prime minister) Simon Harris is due to become taoiseach in November 2027, under the coalition's rotating taoiseach agreement.

His party has now proposed setting up an "independent, government-supported, inter-party and consultative forum" as part of preparations for reunification of the island.

It would be underpinned by law and operate for five years, with the option for a two year extension.

It would be led by an independent chair appointed by the Irish government and have its own secretariat as well as a budget, the party said.

The forum would publish research, reports and recommendations on Irish unity.

Membership of the forum would be open to representatives of all political parties who have elected politicians across the island, who "advocate exclusively through peaceful means".

It would have a panel of academics and other experts to support its work.

"The Forum would commission research, examine constitutional and institutional options, identify areas of agreement and disagreement, and provide recommendations to help build the basis for a Unified Island," Fine Gael's policy paper states.

Fianna Fáil's "initiative" on Irish unity said it would specifically explore three scenarios - a single united Ireland, without devolved governments; a united Ireland with a devolved republic and a third scenario, with no constitutional change.

However, Fine Gael's proposal does not go so far, stating only that the forum would "examine different constitutional models which are compatible with different economic approaches".

The forum would, however, look at the "future" of the institutions in Northern Ireland and the "possible subsequent reform of local and regional government on an all-island basis in line with the European principle of subsidiarity".

It would also examine the changes needed in Ireland's institutions, as well as public taxation, healthcare, education and other public services and practical requirements.

The forum would also look at "protections for British identity" which includes citizenship, cultural expression, rights and political representation as well as "the rights and identities of all communities – flags, emblems and anthems".

It would also examine security and defence as currently there are different policies both in the Republic of Ireland and in Northern Ireland.

In one of the first hints as to what Harris' second tenure as taoiseach may look like as he takes on the role this time next year, Fine Gael also proposes to appoint a junior minister for "north south relations".

The appointment would be made by the taoiseach and the party wants to transfer responsibility for "long term constitutional planning" from the Irish Department of Foreign Affairs to the Department of Taoiseach.

In his speech at the party conference on Saturday, Harris said "Fine Gael's commitment to a united Ireland is enduring"

"We are the United Ireland party," he continued.

"But that commitment must be matched by serious preparation, practical proposals and a willingness to engage with people of all traditions on this island."

How much could a United Ireland cost to Irish taxpayers?

On the question of the cost of a united Ireland, Fine Gael has tasked Stephen Kinsella, an economist who is an adviser to Harris and a professor at the University of Limerick, to examine the issue.

He undertook findings which have been published alongside the party's Irish unity "blueprint".

Kinsella suggests that the first-year cost of reunification ranges from about €3bn (£2.5bn) to €25bn (£20.8) to the Irish exchequer, depending on what Irish unity looks like, what is agreed with the UK and how much it costs to bring Northern Ireland pay and welfare to the same levels as that in the Republic of Ireland.

In a scenario he calls "managed integration", he said year one of a united Ireland could cost between €4bn (£3.3bn) and €4.7bn (£3.9) to the Irish taxpayer if the UK keeps pensions and debt interest.

Kinsella said this could rise to between €13.6bn (£11.3bn) and €14.2bn (£11.8bn) if Dublin has to pay pensions and debt interest.

articles.body: One of the world's most popular fan fiction libraries has been offline for over a week after a cyberattack, denying millions of fans access to their favourite stories. Archive of Our Own, known as AO3, has displayed a maintenance message since Oct 29. Launched in 2008, the platform has over 11 million registered users and nearly 18 million works. Operator Organization for Transformative Works said it did not believe its user database, containing usernames, email IDs and passwords, was stolen, but could not rule this out. articles.title: Psychology says people who enjoy being alone often share these traits: Why they value their own company, enjoy quiet time and build meaningful relationships
articles.summary: Being alone on a Friday evening does not always mean someone has no plans, friends or social life.
articles.body: Being alone on a Friday evening does not always mean someone has no plans, friends or social life. For some people, it is a choice they genuinely look forward to. They may happily watch a film alone, take a solo trip, spend hours reading or simply enjoy a quiet afternoon without feeling the need to call someone. In a world where socialising, constant messages and online connections often fill our days, choosing one's own company can seem unusual. It is also easy to mistake people who enjoy solitude for those who are lonely, withdrawn or uncomfortable around others. But the two experiences are not the same.Psychology research suggests that the way people experience time alone depends partly on why they choose it. A 2022 study published in PLOS ONE, titled "Who enjoys solitude? Autonomous functioning (but not introversion) predicts self-determined motivation (but not preference) for solitude", explored this question through two diary studies involving university students. Researchers found that dispositional autonomy, or the ability to make choices based on personal interests rather than outside pressure, was linked to enjoying time alone for its own benefits. Interestingly, introversion did not predict this motivation.So, what might people who enjoy their own company have in common? Here are some behaviours often associated with positive solitude, although they do not apply to everyone.1. They are comfortable making their own choicesPeople who enjoy solitude may not wait for company to do something they want. They can go to a restaurant, watch a film, visit an exhibition or plan a weekend getaway on their own. Their plans do not always depend on whether friends or family are available. This can also make them more flexible. They may decide to explore a new place at short notice or spend an evening pursuing an interest without having to coordinate with a group.Another quality that may accompany this preference is emotional independence. Such individuals may feel less pressure to seek approval for every decision and find satisfaction in activities they choose for themselves. This does not mean they never need support or value other people's opinions. Rather, they may be comfortable making decisions without relying on constant reassurance from others.2. They make room for reflection and personal interestsQuiet time can offer an opportunity to pause and understand what is happening within. Some people use these moments to think about their experiences, recognise their emotions and reflect on decisions they have made. Their preferred activities may include reading, writing, meditation, solving puzzles or exploring creative interests. These hobbies offer mental stimulation while allowing them to work at their own pace.For some, writing helps organise thoughts, while reading provides an opportunity to explore new ideas. Others may enjoy painting, music or strategy games because these activities allow them to concentrate without interruption. However, spending time alone does not automatically make someone more self-aware or emotionally intelligent. The value of reflection depends on how a person uses that time.3. Nature and pets can become comforting companionsA walk through a forest, a quiet afternoon by the sea or a solo trek in the mountains can make solitude especially enjoyable. Natural surroundings may give people a break from busy schedules, notifications and everyday demands. Some also enjoy having pets around during their alone time. A dog resting beside them or a cat sitting nearby can offer companionship and affection without requiring the same kind of conversation as human relationships.For these individuals, being alone does not necessarily mean feeling disconnected. They may simply find comfort in quieter surroundings and activities that allow them to slow down. Still, a preference for solitude does not automatically mean someone loves nature, owns pets or has stronger environmental values. These are personal interests, not fixed personality traits.4. They value meaningful relationships over constant interactionEnjoying time alone does not mean avoiding relationships. Many people who appreciate solitude maintain close friendships, spend time with family and enjoy social gatherings. The difference may lie in how they balance these interactions with their need for personal space. Some prefer smaller conversations over large gatherings. They may listen carefully, think before responding and take time to build connections rather than seeking frequent social interaction. Others stay in touch through messages and online platforms, while choosing in-person meetings when they genuinely want to spend time with someone.They may also be more conscious of their personal boundaries. Whether it is following a morning routine, exercising alone or setting aside time to relax, they make room for activities that help them feel comfortable. However, being reserved does not automatically make someone a better listener or more thoughtful friend. These qualities vary from person to person.5. They understand that solitude is different from lonelinessPerhaps the most important distinction is that choosing to be alone is not the same as feeling isolated. Voluntary solitude can feel peaceful and refreshing, while unwanted isolation may leave someone feeling disconnected. A study published in Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin in 2023 examined the relationship between daily solitude and well-being through a 21-day diary study involving 178 participants. It found that spending more time alone was associated with lower satisfaction and greater loneliness on some days. However, when solitude was chosen freely and did not continue accumulating over days, these negative associations were reduced or disappeared. Participants also reported lower stress and greater feelings of autonomy on days when they spent more time alone.A 2025 review in the Journal of Personality also highlighted that solitude can appeal to people with different personality types. Its benefits depend on factors such as why someone chooses to be alone, the situation and what they do with that time. Ultimately, enjoying your own company is not a personality test or proof that someone is more independent, intelligent or emotionally mature. Some people recharge through social interaction, while others find the same comfort in quiet moments. Both are perfectly valid. The important difference is whether time alone feels like a choice that brings satisfaction or an experience someone wishes they could escape. When it is freely chosen, solitude can make room for reflection, personal interests and a healthier balance between individual needs and relationships.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
